chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Abu Abdullah al-Razi narrated to me, from Ali ibn Suleiman ibn Rashid, from Musa ibn Salam, from Aban ibn Savid, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked: What is that which stabilizes faith in the servant? He replied: That which stabilizes it in him is piety (al-wara'), and that which removes it from him is greed (al-tama').
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual causes that stabilize or remove faith in a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Aban ibn Suwayd queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the spiritual mechanics of faith, receiving a concise answer that identifies *al-wara'* (scrupulous piety) as the stabilizing force and *al-tama'* (insatiable greed) as the destructive element. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *wara'* not merely as avoidance of the doubtful, but as the active preservation of the heart’s conviction against the corrupting influence of worldly desire.
